deities: Lord Shiva as Pashupatinath (named for Pashupatinath of Kathmandu; the murti/architecture of this shrine is unsourced)

history.summary: IDENTITY: verified as entry #7 'Mangan Pashupatinath Mandir', location 'Mangan Bazaar', on the Sikkim Ecclesiastical Department's official district-wise list of Hindu mandirs - it is a real Shiva shrine in Mangan town. No independent web source (place listings, directories, news) mentions it, so its architecture, age and management are undocumented. The name indicates it is inspired by Kathmandu's Pashupatinath (a major pilgrimage link for the Nepali-Hindu community of Sikkim); whether it is a deliberate replica or simply a namesake is unverified. Coordinates are a Mangan-town fallback only - approximate, flagged.

name: Mangan Pashupatinath Mandir
town_description: Mangan is the headquarters of Mangan district (North Sikkim), about 65 km from Gangtok, and the base town for travel into North Sikkim (Lachung, Lachen, Gurudongmar Lake), set above the Teesta river valley.

travel.airport: Bagdogra Airport, West Bengal, about 146 km via Rangpo-Singtam-Dikchu (per darjeeling-tourism.com; verify).
travel.railway: New Jalpaiguri (NJP) Station, West Bengal, about 138 km (per darjeeling-tourism.com; verify).
travel.road: About 65 km from Gangtok (about 2 hrs 45 min); regular shared jeeps and buses from Gangtok's Vajra taxi stand; the mandir is listed at Mangan Bazaar, in the town itself.

visitor_information.best_time: March to May and October to December, the usual Sikkim season.
